**The solution is to give Clanker a payment tool that completes purchases you approve through Slack.**

The current block comes from our implementation: Clanker’s policy says payment is owner-only, and its payment handlers are disabled. The old card executor was removed during the Kernel migration. Sending you back to the sign-in link was also a broken checkout handoff. [Current policy](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/clanker_policy.py:4), [disabled handlers](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/payments.py:5).

Kernel **does support payments**, including protected card filling and wallet integrations. Clanker needs to integrate that capability. [Kernel payment documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/payments).

The flow I recommend is:

1. **Clanker prepares checkout** and shows the verified merchant, items, delivery details and final total in Slack.
2. **You approve that exact purchase**, for example “Pay ₹69.” Approval belongs to your account and that checkout; changed totals require fresh approval.
3. **Clanker completes checkout** through Kernel’s payment integration. Card enrollment and any required bank authentication use a secure private link opened from Slack. You don’t operate Clanker’s browser.
4. **Clanker verifies the merchant’s order record** and returns the confirmation. An uncertain result triggers reconciliation before another payment attempt.

**For your India use case, I’d evaluate Kernel + AgentCard first.** It uses placeholder card values while the real card stays outside the agent’s browser, and Kernel documents support for specific Razorpay checkout requests. Kernel’s Link integration currently requires a US phone number. [AgentCard integration](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/agentcard), [Link requirements](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/stripe-link).

So saving a card alone won’t fix this. We need the wallet integration, purchase approval, payment execution and order verification together. The same approval flow can support COD when the merchant offers it.

**The remaining unknown is whether Zepto’s actual checkout matches a supported payment flow. That needs verification before promising it will work there.**

yeah so all I want to see in the slack dm or channel thread is "pay X" card and then it redirects me to put my card for the first time with the option to remember the card otherwise just ask me the card details all the time. can we do that with the current SOTA ?

**Yes. That experience is achievable today.** Slack supports a **Pay ₹X** button that opens a private payment page. [Slack documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)

The experience we would build:

1. **Clanker posts the purchase card** in your DM or channel thread: merchant, order summary, total and **Pay ₹69**.
2. **First payment:** the button opens a secure card form with an optional **Remember this card** checkbox.
3. **Later payments:** remembered cards appear masked, such as **Visa •••• 1234**, for approval. Otherwise, you enter your card again.
4. **Clanker finishes checkout** and posts the order confirmation in the original thread.

In a channel, the payment page would authenticate the intended payer. Card details stay with the payment provider; Clanker receives references and payment status.

**One qualification to my earlier recommendation:** Kernel + AgentCard already documents hosted card enrollment, remembered cards and purchase approval. Its published enrollment flow stores the card; I haven’t verified a native **“use once without saving”** option. That branch needs confirmed provider support before we promise the exact checkbox behavior. The choice must govern storage at the provider. [Enrollment documentation](https://docs.agentcard.sh/vault/adding-a-card)

Banks may still require OTP or 3DS authentication, and individual merchant checkouts need verification.

**The Slack experience is feasible now. Optional card retention is the specific provider capability still to validate.**
but the card details and shit are handled through vault's payment typed item right>?

**Yes. Kernel Vault handles payments through two typed items:**

- **`wallet`** connects your payment provider and exposes the secure card enrollment flow.
- **`card`** represents the payment material and purchase authorization.

With **AgentCard**, the actual card number and CVV stay with the provider. Kernel supplies placeholder aliases for checkout; Clanker works with item references, approval state and results. [Kernel documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/overview)

That’s the architecture we should use for your **Pay ₹X** Slack card. Clanker needs the integration wired up.

The **“remember this card” checkbox** is the remaining detail: the provider must support optional retention. Vault having a `card` type doesn’t automatically establish that behavior.
I only want to do cards for now

**Cards only for now.** The target flow stays:

1. **Pay ₹X** in Slack.
2. Secure card entry with optional **Remember this card**.
3. Clanker completes checkout and posts confirmation in the same thread.

Kernel’s `wallet` item is simply the connection to the card provider. We still use `wallet` + `card` items while offering only card payments.

The optional “don’t remember” behavior still needs provider verification.
get the provider verification real quick

**Verified: saved cards are supported. A built-in “don’t remember this card” option is not documented.**

1. **AgentCard:** hosted card entry, encrypted storage and reuse are confirmed. Its enrollment API has no documented `remember=false` or temporary-card option. [Enrollment API](https://docs.agentcard.sh/api-reference/vault/sessions-create)

2. **Kernel has a native card provider I missed earlier.** Its live API exposes `provider: "kernel"` with hosted card enrollment and purchase-specific payment tokens. Deleting its wallet also removes the enrolled card. [Live API specification](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json), [deletion behavior](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/api-reference/vaults/delete-a-vault-item-and-invalidate-its-secret-value)

That gives us documented building blocks for:

- **Remember checked:** retain the enrolled card.
- **Unchecked:** temporarily enroll it, then remove it once the payment outcome is resolved. Ask for card details next time.

**Native Kernel’s current limits matter:** the issuer must support its network tokens, and the schema caps purchases at **50,000 minor units, meaning ₹500 for INR**. [Specification](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json)

The “use once, then remove” design is feasible from the published API. Its actual operation with your card and Zepto remains untested.

content.text:
**Kernel’s native provider is real and exposed in its official Python SDK.** It is separate from Link and AgentCard.

- **Enrollment:** one `provider: "kernel"` wallet stores one card. Kernel hosts the card-and-email form; its documentation says the actual card number never reaches Kernel. The card’s issuer must support its agentic network token. No issuer list or India availability guarantee was found. [Official wallet schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)
- **Purchase:** Kernel issues a network token number, expiry and one-time three-digit code bound to the amount. It encrypts those values and fills them only on the declared merchant origin. **Maximum: 50,000 minor units, meaning ₹500 INR**, with INR explicitly supported. Visa requires a Visa passkey approval and merchant country; Mastercard requires no additional hosted approval. Application approval remains necessary. [Official purchase schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)
- **Security boundary:** the original card stays out of the browser, but the network token and one-time code are injected into it. Native Kernel cards **do not use aliases or egress substitution**. Kernel does not observe whether the merchant charged the card. Clanker must verify the order separately. [Official card state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)
- **Removal:** wallet deletion blocks new purchases and removes the enrolled card. Failure retains the blocked wallet for deletion retry; unresolved payment operations can block deletion. Therefore “use once then remove” is a lifecycle we would implement, not a documented native checkbox or zero-retention mode. [Official delete implementation and contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/resources/vaults/items.py)

The general payment guide, wallet narrative docs and public changelog currently emphasize Link and AgentCard. **No official underlying vault vendor, explicit PCI certification, native-provider access gate or geographic support matrix was found.** Avoid claiming any of those.

**Yes, use Kernel’s native `wallet` + `card` entities for eligible cards.** No material correction.

The `wallet` enrolls the original card; each `card` item represents a purchase and provides a network token plus one-time code for Kernel’s origin-bound `fill`. Clanker then submits the merchant checkout and verifies the order record.

Current constraints: **₹500 per INR purchase**, issuer eligibility, Visa passkey approval and unverified Zepto compatibility. The `card` type is a purchase credential, not a generic vault for storing raw card details.

**Egress means the outgoing checkout request as it leaves Kernel’s browser toward the payment processor.** Kernel can inspect that request, check its authorization and replace payment aliases or hold it while AgentCard executes the payment.

**Native `provider: "kernel"` works differently:** its official SDK explicitly says it does not use aliases or egress substitution. It fills an encrypted network token and one-time code into the merchant page; the merchant submits payment. [Native card state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

The blog describes the Link and AgentCard integrations; its egress claim should not be applied to native Kernel cards.

**Native Kernel cards can use a merchant’s existing checkout, but “works everywhere” is unsupported.**

The documented conditions are eligible issuer tokenization, supported currency and amount, origin-bound field filling, unexpired one-time code and Visa passkey approval where required. The merchant’s checkout must still accept and successfully process those credentials. [Wallet schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py), [purchase schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

The native schemas do not document a processor whitelist or guarantee arbitrary website compatibility. Clanker also must confirm the merchant order, because Kernel does not observe whether the merchant charged the card. [Card state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

**Any claim of broader coverage than processor-specific egress adapters is an architectural inference, requiring checkout testing.**

**Native Kernel’s documented flow is enrollment → explicit purchase approval → token authorization → field fill → merchant checkout submission.**

1. **Enroll the card:** `PUT /vaults/{vault}/items/{walletKey}` with `type:"wallet"` and `spec:{provider:"kernel"}` returns a `card_enrollment` URL. The user enters card and email on Kernel’s hosted page. `connected` means stored; payment readiness additionally requires `payment_methods[].capabilities.single_use_card.eligible`. [Wallet specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec_param.py)
2. **Create one purchase:** another item uses `type:"card"`, provider `kernel`, wallet key, merchant name/URL, amount and currency. Visa also requires merchant country. Current maximum is **50,000 minor units: ₹500 INR**. [Purchase specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec_param.py)
3. **Authorize:** after explicit user approval, inspect `available_operations`, then POST `{type:"authorize"}` to `/items/{purchaseKey}/operations`. Visa returns a `spend_approval` URL requiring a Visa passkey; Mastercard has no extra hosted approval. [Authorization contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/authorize_vault_item_operation_request_param.py)
4. **Fill and submit:** once `ready`, invoke advertised `fill` with browser ID, exact current HTTPS page URL and selectors. Kernel writes encrypted network-token credentials, restricted to the merchant origin. Fill does not submit; the controller submits the merchant checkout before `expires_at`. Values remain readable through unrestricted browser access. [Fill contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/fill_vault_item_operation_request_param.py)
5. **Verify the order:** Kernel does not observe the merchant charge. `completed` means fields filled, not paid. `recovery_required` blocks deletion/replacement until the unresolved token/approval operation is reconciled with support. [Card state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py), [fill result](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/fill_vault_item_operation_result.py)

**Issuer eligibility and real merchant acceptance remain checks; native Kernel has no documented universal checkout guarantee.**

**The documented native flow does not require the merchant to adopt Kernel’s checkout workflow.** It fills a network-token number, expiry and one-time code into the merchant’s existing card fields; the merchant’s own checkout submits payment. The native schema has no merchant registration or integration requirement. [Official purchase contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

Declaring `merchant_url` limits where Clanker may use the purchase credential. It is an authorization boundary, not a merchant signup step.

**The remaining uncertainty is acceptance:** the issuer must support token enrollment, and the merchant’s checkout and processor must successfully process the generated credential. The public native contract does not promise universal support. [Enrollment eligibility](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)

**You cannot prove native Kernel works on every website before implementation.** You can validate the relevant card and merchant combinations with a small isolated proof of concept before building the Slack flow.

1. **Check card eligibility:** after authorized enrollment, read the wallet’s advertised `payment_methods` expansion. Require `capabilities.single_use_card.eligible`; retain its reasons. This confirms token eligibility, not merchant acceptance. [Native wallet contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)
2. **Test actual priority merchants:** perform one explicitly approved purchase below ₹500 on each target checkout, exercising authorization, field filling, any authentication and submission. Verify both merchant order confirmation and the payment outcome.
3. **Test failure handling:** confirm expired credentials, origin changes, interrupted authentication and unknown outcomes do not trigger a second payment automatically. [Native card state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)
4. **Record measured coverage:** report tested website/card combinations and known failures. Kernel says filling needs no processor adapter, but does not guarantee processor acceptance or payment success. [Coverage documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/integrations/wallets/overview#checkout-and-processor-coverage)

**No documented native sandbox, native demo or issuer/merchant support matrix was found; the official card schema says test-mode card creation is unsupported.** [Live-card contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/vault_item.py)

All checks here remained read-only; no card enrollment or payment was performed.

**No. The native `provider: "kernel"` flow does not require the user to connect Link or AgentCard.** Its official SDK describes entering a card and email on a Kernel-hosted enrollment page. [Native wallet specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)

The wallet overview currently describes Link and AgentCard only, so there is a documentation gap. Native Kernel exists in the public schema, but **availability for your project and eligibility of your card remain unverified**. No public source reviewed identifies it as preview-only or names its underlying storage provider.
